title: JFrog access token in a Bearer header
summary: A synthetic access token after the Bearer scheme in an Authorization header of a platform request, in a quoted curl -H argument without a space after the option, a raw request and a JSON header map.
rationale: JFrog documents that an access token can be used as a bearer token in the Authorization header. The documentation states no prefix, alphabet or width of the token. A JSON Web Token form is not an exclusive identifying grammar, since the same page documents a reference token as an alias that is used as a Basic password, so no fixture depends on a JWT shape and no bare-value rule is implied. The Bearer scheme is generic, so the attribution stays generic; the extent is the value after the scheme and excludes the closing quote.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, credential-evidence#235). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Flagged under project policy: the value after an explicit Bearer scheme in an Authorization header of a JFrog platform request is treated as a credential and covered whole. JFrog documents the Bearer header form (carrier existence only); the value admission, extent and generic authorization attribution are the project's decisions.

sources.supports: An access token can be used as a bearer token in authorization headers.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.
